contentHtml:
Over 60 students engage with industry and academic leaders on career and research opportunities

The University of Liverpool Bengaluru and Biocon Academy jointly organised a roundtable bringing together senior leaders from academia, healthcare, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and clinical research to explore opportunities for strengthening UK-India collaboration in education, research, healthcare innovation and workforce development. Hosted by Professor Richard Grose, Provost of the University of Liverpool Bengaluru Campus, the roundtable provided a platform for industry and academic stakeholders to discuss potential partnerships across the life sciences sector.

Chaired by Professor Shakila Thangaratinam, Dean of ILCAMS and University Strategic Adviser for Global Engagement and Partnership, the roundtable brought together representatives from Biocon Academy, Syngene, Teva Pharmaceuticals India, All India Co-ordinating Committee, Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, SRM Institutions and the University of Liverpool.

The programme featured keynote contributions from Professor Peter McCormick, Associate Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Postgraduate Affairs and International Partnerships at the University of Liverpool, and Bindu Ajit, Head of Biocon Academy. The speakers shared perspectives on international partnership models, industry-academia collaboration, workforce development and emerging opportunities within the UK-India relationship in healthcare and life sciences.

Discussions explored opportunities to leverage the University of Liverpool’s expertise in drug discovery, women’s health, Artificial Intelligence and clinical trials alongside India’s strengths in biotechnology and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Participants discussed the potential for closer collaboration between academia, industry and healthcare institutions to strengthen research capabilities, accelerate innovation and develop skilled talent across the sector. The roundtable was preceded by a strategic leadership meeting between Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon Group, and the University of Liverpool team.

Professor Thangaratinam said, “The future of healthcare innovation will be shaped by partnerships that transcend traditional boundaries between disciplines, sectors and countries. That belief was the driving force behind the University of Liverpool bringing together leaders from industry, healthcare and academia for this programme. The energy and commitment demonstrated throughout today’s discussions reinforce the enormous potential to create a globally connected life sciences ecosystem that delivers benefits for patients, researchers, students and industry alike.”

Professor Richard Grose, Provost, University of Liverpool Bengaluru, said, “Our focus at the University of Liverpool Bengaluru Campus is on providing students in India with access to a world-class education that equips them with the skills, knowledge and global perspective needed to succeed in rapidly evolving sectors such as healthcare and life sciences. Bringing together leaders from academia, industry and healthcare is an important way of ensuring our programmes remain connected to real-world challenges and opportunities, helping to develop graduates who are ready to make an impact both in India and internationally.”

Professor McCormick said, “International partnerships are increasingly important in addressing complex global challenges and advancing scientific discovery. The strength of the UK-India relationship lies in the complementary expertise, ambition and innovation that both countries bring. The University of Liverpool is committed to building long-term collaborations that create opportunities for students, researchers and industry partners, while contributing to the growth of a globally connected life sciences sector.”

Ajit said, “The future of life sciences depends on our ability to develop globally minded talent with the skills to work across disciplines, technologies and international markets. Collaborations between academia and industry are key to achieving this goal. We were delighted to work with colleagues from the University of Liverpool and the University of Liverpool Bengaluru Campus to explore opportunities for partnership in education, workforce development and innovation. Together, we have an opportunity to create meaningful pathways for the next generation of scientists.”

Following the roundtable, delegates attended an extended networking session with over 60 students from the inaugural cohort of the BSc Biomedical Sciences programme at the University of Liverpool Bengaluru Campus. The session provided students with an opportunity to interact with leaders from academia, healthcare and industry and gain insights into career pathways, research opportunities and developments across the life sciences sector.

The event concluded with a shared commitment to developing collaborative initiatives across biomedical sciences education, clinical research training, Artificial Intelligence for life sciences, healthcare professional development and innovation-led entrepreneurship. The discussions further highlighted opportunities to strengthen UK-India engagement in education, research and innovation while supporting the development of future healthcare and scientific talent.
